taxonomies.tooltip: Sri Lanka's adaptation sectors, as set by the UNDP country office from the country's NDC 3.0 (2026-2035) and the Global Goal on Adaptation
taxonomies._source: Paragraphs attributed to decision 2/CMA.5 equal categories.json gga_categories word for word (paragraph 9(a), (b), (c), (e); https://unfccc.int/sites/default/files/resource/cma2023_16a01E.pdf#page=9). Paragraphs attributed to 'Description in NDC 3.0' are close extracts of Sri Lanka's NDC 3.0 with light edits by the country office (checked 6 Oct 2026 against https://unfccc.int/sites/default/files/2025-09/Sri%20Lankas%20Nationally%20Determined%20Contributions%203.0%20(2026-2035)%20submitted%2022.09.2025%20(1).pdf).

categories.name: Agriculture and food
categories.description:
Attaining climate-resilient food and agricultural production and supply and distribution of food, as well as increasing sustainable and regenerative production and equitable access to adequate food and nutrition for all

Also includes managing climate risks to improve productivity and ensure food security of the country, integrated Pest Management, and Integrated Plant Nutrition Management Systems.
categories._documentRow: Agriculture (called Agriculture and food for Sri Lanka)

categories.name: Livestock
categories.description: Efforts to introduce adaptation measures in the livestock sector, particularly genetic improvement, disease surveillance and forage improvement strategies to address climate impacts on ruminant livestock. It also includes technological innovations and interventions, especially by improved feeding, disease surveillance and management strategies, to build resilience in poultry and swine farming, and research and education in livestock.

categories.name: Fisheries
categories.description: Targeting vulnerability reduction, capacity building, technology transfer, and institutional coordination to protect fisheries-dependent livelihoods from climate risks. Includes Ecosystem-based Approach to Fisheries Management, climate-resilient varieties and farming and breeding technologies.

categories.name: Biodiversity
categories.description: Tackles land degradation and soil conservation and promotes ecosystem protection, genetic diversity conservation, and inclusive stakeholder involvement. Can include Identification, mapping and management of areas that are highly vulnerable to adverse impact of climate change, protected areas and increased connectivity, and the management of the spread of Invasive Alien Species.

categories.name: Health
categories.description:
Attaining resilience against climate change related health impacts, promoting climate-resilient health services and significantly reducing climate-related morbidity and mortality, particularly in the most vulnerable communities

Integrated, resilience-focused approach that prioritizes climate-resilient health systems, strengthened disease surveillance and early warning systems, improved health infrastructure, and enhanced institutional and community capacity to adapt to evolving climate risks.

categories.name: Tourism
categories.description:
Tourism policies, complemented by environmental and aviation laws, such as support climate adaptation through global and national sustainable tourism certification, strategic planning, and environmental protection to mitigate risks from climate hazards affecting infrastructure and biodiversity.

Risk reduction and transfer mechanisms are integral to this approach, encompassing improved early warning systems, capacity-building programmes, green building design, climate change awareness and educational programmes in the tourism, and coastal protection initiatives.

categories.name: Infrastructure and human settlements
categories.description:
Increasing the resilience of infrastructure and human settlements to climate change impacts to ensure basic and continuous essential services for all, and minimizing climate-related impacts on infrastructure and human settlements

Regulations emphasizing environmental compliance, flood risk reduction, and sustainable infrastructure development in urban areas. Integrating climate adaptation into land-use planning and urban development
categories._documentRow: Urban Planning and Human settlements (called Infrastructure and human settlements in Sri Lanka)

categories.name: Water
categories.description:
Significantly reducing climate-induced water scarcity and enhancing climate resilience to water-related hazards towards a climate-resilient water supply, climate-resilient sanitation and access to safe and affordable potable water for all.

Aims to secure sustainable water management critical for agriculture, human consumption, and ecological health amidst climatic uncertainties.

categories.name: Coastal and marine
categories.description: Integrated coastal resource management, encompassing ecosystem protection and restoration, development regulation, and community safeguards against sea-level rise and extreme events. Focuses on protecting coastal ecosystems and communities from sea-level rise and extreme weather events.

taxonomies.tooltip: Loss and damage, as set by the UNDP country office from Sri Lanka's NDC 3.0 (2026-2035)
taxonomies._source: Paragraphs 2 and 3 are close extracts of the loss and damage section of Sri Lanka's NDC 3.0 (PDF page 79). Paragraph 1, the definition and the caveat that a loss is not automatically attributable to climate change, does not appear in NDC 3.0 (checked 6 Oct 2026); the document attributes it there, and it is kept as country-office text (Jonas Nothnagel, 6 Oct 2026). https://unfccc.int/sites/default/files/2025-09/Sri%20Lankas%20Nationally%20Determined%20Contributions%203.0%20(2026-2035)%20submitted%2022.09.2025%20(1).pdf

categories.name: Loss and damage
categories.description:
Loss and Damage refers to economic and non-economic adverse impacts and risks associated with climate change, including those arising from extreme weather events and slow-onset processes, which are not, or cannot be, fully avoided through mitigation, adaptation and disaster risk reduction. This framing does not imply that every disaster-related loss is automatically attributable to climate change; the climate rationale should be established through available scientific evidence, observed trends and climate projections.

Targeted interventions for climate change adaptation and resilience building to reduce disaster-related losses and damages and to plan for recovery from residual impacts. This approach emphasizes the need for a comprehensive, multi- dimensional strategy that integrates risk management and capacity building.

Key actions include assessing disaster impacts, improving early warning and data collection systems for L&D, strengthening institutional coordination across all levels, and leveraging existing integrated L&D frameworks to support effective implementation, compensation, and recovery efforts.
